title: Contraction deletion agrees with suspended bar faces
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention] and tensor and cochain conventions as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small dg category over $\mathbf Z$: its mapping objects are cochain complexes with associative unital chain-map composition. Let $\mathcal A$ be a full dg subcategory and $X,Y$ objects of $\mathcal C$. For $n\geq0$ let $V_n$ be the direct sum, over $A_0,\ldots,A_n\in\mathcal A$, of
$$\mathcal C(A_n,Y)\otimes\mathcal A(A_{n-1},A_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal A(A_0,A_1)\otimes\mathcal C(X,A_0),$$
with $V_0=\bigoplus_{A_0}\mathcal C(A_0,Y)\otimes\mathcal C(X,A_0)$. Let $W_n$ be the corresponding graded tensor sums with a formal rank-one degree-$-1$ generator $\varepsilon_{A}$ inserted at each of the $n+1$ intermediate objects; write their pure tensors as words $a_0\varepsilon_{A_n}a_1\cdots a_n\varepsilon_{A_0}a_{n+1}$. These are tensors, with no balanced relations. Define the graded isomorphism $\Phi_n:V_n[n+1]\to W_n$ by multiplying each such word by $(-1)^{\alpha_n}$, where $\alpha_n=n+\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(n+1-j)|a_j|$. For $n\geq1$, define $\partial_i:V_n\to V_{n-1}$, $0\leq i\leq n$, by composing factors $a_i,a_{i+1}$ and omitting their shared intermediate object. Define the degree-$1$ map $D_{\rm del}:W_n\to W_{n-1}$ on each homogeneous word as the sum of these separator deletions, composing adjacent factors, with coefficient $(-1)^{S_i-i}$ for deletion number $i$ from the left, where $S_i=\sum_{j=0}^{i}|a_j|$. For $n=0$, define $D_{\rm del}:W_0\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$ by the same rule, deleting the sole separator and composing. All formulas extend to the tensor sums as homomorphisms, and
$$\Phi_{n-1}^{-1}D_{\rm del}\Phi_n=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^{i+1}\partial_i\quad(n\geq1),\qquad D_{\rm del}\Phi_0=\mathrm{ev},$$
where $\mathrm{ev}:V_0\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$ is composition. The first equality is between degree-$1$ maps from $V_n[n+1]$ to $V_{n-1}[n]$. The formulas are natural under dg functors carrying the chosen objects and full subcategory into corresponding data. They require no flatness, pretriangulatedness, or quotient universal property.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 3.1 (differential obtained from d(epsilon_U)=id_U), section 3.2 and section 3.6(i); agent-explicit all-length deletion/face and augmentation sign calculation. No Stacks tag states this dg-word comparison.

proof.text: Fix a homogeneous pure tensor in the summand indexed by $(A_0,\ldots,A_n)$ and write $d_j=|a_j|$. Deleting the separator numbered $i$ (the separator immediately after $a_i$) replaces the adjacent pair by $b_i=a_i a_{i+1}$ and produces the corresponding pure tensor in the $(n-1)$-summand; its degree is $|b_i|=d_i+d_{i+1}$ by graded composition. Thus the $i$-th term is exactly $(-1)^{S_i-i}$ times that output word, with no balanced relation involved. On each fixed multidegree the sign is constant and composition is bilinear, so the displayed formulas respect the tensor bilinearity relations and define homomorphisms. Taking the direct sum over multidegrees and object tuples defines the maps on all tensors. Removing the formal rank-one generators and multiplying by the same sign gives the inverse of $\Phi_n$, since $(-1)^{2\alpha_n}=1$. A word has degree $\sum_jd_j-(n+1)$; deleting a degree-$-1$ separator raises this degree by one, including at $n=0$.

source.place: Drinfeld, section 3.1: the differential of a word after adjoining generators with $d(\varepsilon_A)=1_A$; agent-explicit identification of the $i$-th deleted separator.

proof.text: Let $\alpha_n=n+\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(n+1-j)d_j$ and let $\alpha_{n-1}^{(i)}$ be the exponent for the output word with $a_i,a_{i+1}$ replaced by $b_i$. Comparing coefficients gives $\alpha_n-\alpha_{n-1}^{(i)}=1+\sum_{j=0}^{i}d_j=1+S_i$: the indices before $i$ each lose one in their coefficient, the merged pair contributes $d_i$, and all later coefficients agree. Therefore the total coefficient after applying $\Phi_n$, deleting the separator, and applying $\Phi_{n-1}^{-1}$ is $(-1)^{\alpha_n+S_i-i-\alpha_{n-1}^{(i)}}=(-1)^{i+1}$, since exponents are taken modulo $2$.

source.place: Drinfeld sections 3.1 and 3.6(i); explicit Koszul-sign calculation for the suspension identification.

proof.text: The preceding calculation holds for every homogeneous pure tensor and every $0\le i\le n$. Such tensors generate each tensor summand, and direct-sum elements have finite support, so additivity gives the identity on $V_n[n+1]$. Summing over $i$ gives $\Phi_{n-1}^{-1}D_{\rm del}\Phi_n=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^{i+1}\partial_i$ for every $n\ge1$. For a dg functor $F$, the induced tensor map sends each factor $a_j$ to $F(a_j)$ and each separator to the separator at $F(A)$. It preserves degrees, hence all sign exponents, and $F(a_i a_{i+1})=F(a_i)F(a_{i+1})$. Thus it commutes with every deletion, every face, and $\Phi_n$ on generators. These equalities extend additively even if distinct object tuples have the same image, proving the asserted naturality.

source.place: Drinfeld section 3.6(i): word differential and functoriality; summation over all contraction positions.

proof.text: For $n=0$ there are two factors $a_0,a_1$ and one separator. Here $\alpha_0=d_0$ and $S_0=d_0$, so the coefficient of the composite after $D_{\rm del}\Phi_0$ is $(-1)^{d_0+d_0}=1$. The resulting map is precisely composition $\mathrm{ev}:V_0\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$, proving $D_{\rm del}\Phi_0=\mathrm{ev}$. A dg functor preserves composition, so this endpoint equality is natural as well.

source.place: Drinfeld section 3.6(i): augmentation/evaluation at bar degree zero; agent-explicit endpoint sign check.
